text: Every time you hit 'update' on your phone or computer, it's gigabytes. You just wanted a tiny bug fixed, not a whole new operating system!
You imagine a small patch, a single line of code changed, sent quickly to your device. Why does it feel like a complete re-download?
The truth is, software isn't a simple single file. It's built like a massive, intricate stack of interconnected components and libraries.
Even a small tweak might touch fundamental layers, forcing large sections to be entirely re-compiled and re-packaged to guarantee compatibility.
Then add new features, which aren't just 'glued on' but are deeply integrated, expanding the entire underlying architecture.
So your tiny update is actually a new, stable version of the whole complex system, re-sent to ensure everything still works together perfectly.
